body:
Sessio is destroyed after calling logout method tahts why you dont see any flash messages after redirect

You can call `Yii::$app->user->logout(false);` if you dont want to session will be destroyed
But i am unsure is it right way or not

I thought that as soon as you call:-
Yii::$app->session->setFlash(...
It automatically creates a new session?
So logout kills the 'user' session, but setting flash message immediately afterwards will create a new session for basic application functionality.

If I use Yii::$app->user->logout(false);. Does it still retain private information about the user (like username, email etc.)?  Or just their publically available info (like ip, browser etc.)?

I don't want the users info to remain in the session (delete it all when they logout), I just want to be able to display flash messages after they have done so (logout).
Is this doable?

Thanx for the reply.
If it doesnt work for you please write which version of yii do you use and show us full version of your action

Can someone else confirm this is the case with a fresh install of the advanced app please?  If it doesn't behave for you as I've described above, I'll continue looking into my environment (which is windows 7 running wempserver 'nginx').

Thanx again for any confirmations / rebuttles.

Verified.
Updated my app that worked correctly, using composer update (had to change "bower-asset-library": "vendor/bower" to "bower-asset-library": "vendor/bower-asset") in my composer.json. Now the flash message doesn't get displayed when the user logs out.
So it worked on Yii 2.0.6 and is broken in current dev version of 2.0.7?
Is that when the bower asset directory name changed? (2.0.6 - 2.0.7)

Sorry @SilverFire.
The previous version could be earlier than 2.0.6...*unsure.
But regardless.  Yes. In the current version 2.0.7, with default download of advanced app & only applying setFlash on login / logout, logout fails to render flash message.

> Is that when the bower asset directory name changed? (2.0.6 - 2.0.7)

that name should not have changed, if it did it was not caused by yii, but maybe by a composer update that broke it.

Just today I got the 60 day warning about Composer needing an update.  I applied that update 'before' updating the working application.
I did this using 'composer self-update,' then had to change my composer.json as described above, before 'composer update' would update the application without error.
Since we don't have better ideas, I think we can do as @klimov-paul suggested
